correctness.rationale: Set t=br, u=y/x and A=b−1−bd. On the given parameter surface the ratio equation factors as u′=u(1−tu)(x+A/(1+u)). Thus u=1/t is invariant; in fact the coefficient of x forces this slope for any invariant positive ray. The restricted equation is x′=x(κ−x); κ>0 gives forward convergence at every x>0 on the ray. The linearization in (x,u) is triangular, with entries −κ and −κ−tA/(1+t)=b[d+r−2br(1−d)]/(1+t). When the latter is positive, local stable manifold uniqueness and backward uniqueness of a trajectory that eventually enters that local manifold exclude all off-ray initial points in the quadrant. I independently solved the two nullclines using w=x/(x+y), checked the printed inequalities at the rational witness, and obtained eigenvalues −9/1100 and 18/275 at E1 and trace −963171/7896100 and determinant 1260441/98701250 at the stated E2. Thus the local-attraction sign is verified directly from the vector field. Bounded exact arithmetic: independent_checks.py 1. No conclusion about an entire attraction-basin boundary or cases with κ≤0 or zero transverse eigenvalue.
